articles.title: Clinical outcomes and toxicity after proton- versus photon-based spatially fractionated radiotherapy for soft-tissue sarcoma: a retrospective cohort
articles.summary: This study evaluates the use of proton-based spatially fractionated radiotherapy for soft-tissue sarcomas. It specifically investigates whether proton Bragg peak advantages effectively reduce low-dose exposure compared to photon-based methods while assessing potential impacts on perioperative wound complications.

articles.title: Personalized dosimetry for targeted radionuclide therapy: initial clinical experience from a case series at a tertiary cancer center
articles.summary: Researchers report on the implementation of personalized dosimetry within routine clinical practice. The study highlights how this approach enhances therapeutic precision by identifying undertreated lesions and improving the protection of organs at risk.

articles.title: Federated learning in cancer imaging: a comprehensive review and future outlook
articles.summary: This review examines the potential of federated learning to overcome data privacy challenges in AI medical model development. It discusses how these techniques can facilitate multi-institutional collaboration to improve cancer imaging and diagnostic accuracy without compromising sensitive patient data.

articles.title: Early toxicity and dosimetry compliance of hypofractionated vs. conventional fractionated comprehensive regional nodes irradiation in breast cancer (HARVEST)
articles.summary: This study evaluated hypofractionated radiotherapy (HF-RT) with regional node irradiation (RNI) against conventional fractionation. Researchers found comparable acute toxicity and cosmesis, suggesting that HF-RT is a feasible option with good protocol compliance in this setting.

articles.title: Particle therapy for T3N0M0 non-small cell lung cancer: a Japanese nationwide prospective registry study
articles.summary: A prospective registry study demonstrates encouraging survival outcomes and low severe toxicity rates for particle therapy in patients with T3N0M0 non-small cell lung cancer. The findings highlight proton or carbon ion therapy as a viable definitive treatment for patients who are medically inoperable or decline surgery.

articles.title: Interpretable Prediction of Lymphopenia Following Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy for rectal Cancer
articles.summary: Researchers analyzed data from the ARISTOTLE phase 3 trial to identify factors contributing to treatment-related lymphopenia. The study highlights how therapy-related changes impact lymphocyte depletion and subsequent progression-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.

articles.title: AI model integrating dosimetric and radiomic features for predicting cognitive impairment after brain radiotherapy
articles.summary: This study developed and validated a multimodal AI model combining dosimetric parameters with MRI-derived radiomics to predict cognitive impairment risks post-brain radiotherapy. Such predictive tools may eventually allow for personalized neuroprotective interventions and adaptive treatment planning.

articles.title: Multimodal Deep Learning Prognostic Model for Predicting Treatment Outcomes for Oropharyngeal Carcinoma
articles.summary: A new deep learning model utilizing cross-attention mechanisms was shown to outperform unimodal approaches in predicting locoregional recurrence for oropharyngeal carcinoma patients. The integration of clinical and CT imaging data suggests potential for improving individualized treatment decision-making.

articles.title: Monte Carlo (TOPAS) characterization of a proton therapy OBI: Automated source parameter optimization and analysis of CBCT acquisition dynamics
articles.summary: This study demonstrates an automated framework for developing high-fidelity Monte Carlo beam models using standard CTDI measurements. The method provides an accessible alternative for characterizing On-Board Imaging (OBI) systems in proton therapy with high dosimetric accuracy.

articles.title: Unsupervised deep learning model for fast energy layer pre-selection of delivery-efficient proton arc therapy plan optimization of nasopharyngeal carcinoma
articles.summary: This research introduces an unsupervised deep learning model designed to pre-select energy layers for proton arc therapy. The approach aims to reduce energy layer switching times and optimize treatment delivery efficiency for complex cases like nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

articles.title: Dose-time-response relationships between radiation dose to the circulating blood and temporal changes in peripheral blood biomarkers during chemoradiation of non-small cell lung cancer
articles.summary: This research analyzes the relationship between radiation exposure to circulating blood and hematological toxicity in lung cancer patients. The findings support the need to minimize blood dose during radiotherapy to reduce treatment-related side effects.

articles.title: Comparison of dose escalation strategies for head and neck cancer patients using a radiobiological model of reoxygenation
articles.summary: This study evaluates different strategies for dose escalation to address tumor hypoxia in head and neck cancers. It provides a radiobiological model to quantify the limitations of dose-escalation approaches in a dynamic tumor environment.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: The BayCare Proton Center has successfully initiated patient treatments using the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie solution. This installation marks a new technological implementation in a clinical setting for advanced proton delivery.

articles.title: 50 million Americans live in counties without a radiation oncology clinic, study finds
articles.summary: A recent study highlights that 50 million Americans reside in counties lacking a radiation oncology clinic, underscoring significant geographic disparities in access to cancer care. The findings emphasize the ongoing challenges in providing equitable radiation treatment coverage across the United States.

articles.title: ASTRO updates guideline on shorter-course radiation therapy for localized prostate cancer
articles.summary: The American Society for Radiation Oncology (ASTRO) has updated its clinical guidelines regarding the use of shorter-course radiation therapy for patients with localized prostate cancer. The update reflects evolving clinical evidence on hypofractionated treatment regimens.

articles.title: IBA treats first patient in clinical trial of FLASH proton therapy for head and neck cancer
articles.summary: IBA has announced the treatment of the first patient in the C-FLASH-01 clinical trial, evaluating the safety and efficacy of ConformalFLASH proton therapy. This trial marks a significant milestone in testing ultra-high dose rate radiation delivery for head and neck cancer patients.

articles.title: Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute opens new wellness space
articles.summary: The Hampton University Proton Cancer Institute has inaugurated a new wellness facility dedicated to supporting patients and their caregivers. This regional development enhances the supportive care infrastructure at this key proton therapy center in the DMV area.

articles.title: Medicare change could cost standalone proton therapy centers millions
articles.summary: A proposed Medicare reimbursement change could reduce payments to independent proton therapy centers by nearly 30% compared to hospital-based facilities. Advocacy groups warn that this pricing shift threatens the financial sustainability of community-based proton centers and may limit patient access to specialized cancer care.
